title: Turks
capsule: In the Chu and Ili river valleys of Zhetysu (Semirechye), the window 666–757 covers the decline of Western Turkic power and the rise of the Türgesh Khaganate, a successor polity drawn from the Duolu wing of the On Oq ("Ten Arrows") confederation. After the Tang dynasty broke the Western Turkic Khaganate around 657, the Türgesh asserted independence under Wushile (Uchelik) Qaghan, who founded their dynasty in 699 and made Suyab in the Chu valley his principal residence, capturing it from the Tang in 703. The khaganate became the chief steppe power resisting the Umayyad Arab advance into Transoxiana, especially under Suluk Qaghan (716–738), while also contending with the Second Turkic Khaganate to the east and recurring civil war between its Kara (Black) and Sary (Yellow) factions. This Türgesh ascendancy, rather than the earlier Western Turkic empire, is the polity that actually held this region across the dataset window.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The steppe extent of the Western Turkic Khaganate is reconstructed from Chinese dynastic histories (Sui shu, Tang shu) and Sogdian documents; core territories in the Ili and Chu valleys are reasonably established, but peripheral nomadic frontiers are broadly estimated and seasonal in character.
